prediction.likelyOutcome: KKS Properties will recover just compensation for the 9.5-acre direct taking at a per-acre rate the court sets somewhere between the State's $45,000/acre and claimant's $92,000/acre figures, producing a floor in the roughly $430,000-$875,000 range before any severance damages. Severance damages to the 18.464-acre western remainder remain legally available despite the adverse 'not landlocked' collateral estoppel ruling, but that ruling meaningfully undercuts claimant's strongest 'total loss of value' theory, and no after-taking value or severance figure appears in the materials provided to quantify that component; the actual trial record (not excerpted here) likely contains the number that would push the award above this floor.

outcome.description: After a four-day January 2018 trial the Court of Claims credited the State's appraiser (with its own adjustments, preappropriation value $52,339 per acre or $1,662,810), found the western remainder's post-taking highest and best use was multifamily residential, and awarded KKS $744,500 in direct and consequential damages. The Third Department affirmed the amended judgment on October 29, 2020. (An earlier award of $532,000 had been reversed in 2014.)
